title: An epimorphic row cover of the incoming second graded differential
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $\mathcal B$ a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $I$ be a commuting bicomplex with complex degree in $\mathbf Z$ and resolution degree in $\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Set $R_s=F(I.X(s))$ and $J=\operatorname{flip}(\operatorname{mappedFunctor}(F)(I))$, extending the resolution degree by zero [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation]. Let $L$ be a decreasing filtration of $\operatorname{Tot}(J)$ by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration] whose degreewise steps agree with the second filtration of $J$. Fix $r\in\mathbf N$ with $0<r$, $s\in\mathbf Z$, and $n=s+r$. Write $m:(L^s\operatorname{Tot}(J))^n\to\operatorname{Tot}(J)^n$ for the inclusion and $q:(L^s\operatorname{Tot}(J))^n\to(\operatorname{gr}^s L)^n$ for the graded projection [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Suppose $a:R_s^r\to(L^s\operatorname{Tot}(J))^n$ satisfies $a m=\epsilon_r^{-1}\iota_{r,s}$, where $\epsilon_r$ is the canonical extension-by-zero term isomorphism and $\iota_{r,s}$ is the diagonal total coprojection. Then there is an epimorphism $e:R_s^{\operatorname{prev}(r)}\to(\operatorname{gr}^s L)^{n-1}$ satisfying $e\delta=d_{R_s}^{\operatorname{prev}(r),r}a q$, where $\delta$ is the incoming differential of the graded complex. Here $\operatorname{prev}$ is the predecessor for the shape $\operatorname{up}\mathbf N$, and $\operatorname{prev}(r)=r-1$ because $r>0$. No assumption $s\geq0$, cycle comparison, boundary subobject, or homology quotient is involved.

proof.text: Write r=k+1 using positivity, so prev(r)=k and n-1=s+k. Each diagonal inclusion whose second index lies in [p,n] has image below L.complexStep p n by hL and the finite-supremum formula. Factor it through the monic degreewise step inclusion. In degree n-1 take the distinguished lift b0 at second index s, precompose with the inverse extension isomorphism at k, and compose with the graded projection to define e.

Prove that lifts of the diagonal inclusions indexed by [s,n-1] jointly detect maps from the step: the equalizer of two maps agreeing on these lifts has image, after the step inclusion, containing every generating image, hence the whole step image; its inclusion is split epic. To prove e epic, first cancel the epic graded projection and then use this detection statement. On the summand s the equality is precisely equality after e (cancel the extension isomorphism). Every other index in [s,n-1] is at least s+1; lift it through the next step and use monicity to identify its step-s lift with that lift followed by the step inclusion. Its graded class is zero by the cokernel condition. This uses no lower bound on s or nonzero-row assumption and needs no inverse graded comparison.

Lift the diagonal inclusion at (k,s+1) in target degree n through L.step(s+1). Expand the total differential into its two components using total_d, iota_D1, iota_D2, d1_eq and d2_eq. The first component is the extended row differential, which conjugates to the row differential by extend_d_eq. The second is (-1)^k times the differential raising s, followed by the diagonal inclusion at (k,s+1). Cancel the monic target step-s inclusion, use naturality of its complex arrow, the prescribed equation for a, and the equation for the step-(s+1) lift, to obtain the corresponding equality inside step s. Compose with the graded projection: the signed second component vanishes by cokernel.condition. Naturality of the quotient complex morphism then gives the required differential square.

proof_origin.note: W4 proves the incoming-row cover completely using finite-supremum generators and equalizer cancellation for epimorphy, then the total-differential calculation and the cokernel condition. This expands the omitted proof of Tag 0130 clause 2 without first-quadrant vanishing in the complex index; all helpers are proved privately in the assigned module.
